claim: Public field selection is inverted. `IsPublicReadWrite` keeps only `readonly` fields (`field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst`). As a result, ordinary public mutable fields of T are silently left out of the contractless formatter, which loses data on round-trip. Public `readonly` fields are included instead, so the generated code tries to assign to them on deserialize. This breaks the criterion 'contractless behaviour over public members', and it contradicts the attribute docs and README ('every public, read-write instance property and field').

claim: Attributes on T are never honoured. When no SurrogateType is set, the collector always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type). It ignores [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] and [DataContract]/[DataMember] on T, so members excluded by T's own contract are still serialized under name keys. This misses the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured'. It also misses the maintainer rule that contractless applies only when T has no [DataContract] or [MessagePackObject].

claim: IsPublicReadWrite has its field check inverted: `field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst` should be `!field.IsReadOnly && !field.IsConst`. In contractless mode a plain public mutable field (`public int MutableField;`) is silently left out of serialization, which breaks the requirement that public members are serialized. A `public readonly` field is included and marked writable, so the generated Deserialize assigns to a readonly field and the formatter fails to compile (CS0191). Surrogate mode uses the same predicate, so a surrogate keyed on a mutable field gets MsgPack022, while one keyed on a readonly field produces uncompilable code.

claim: The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. When no surrogate is given, Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers and never reads [MessagePackObject], [Key] or [IgnoreMember] on T. A referenced type with `[MessagePackObject] class Data { [Key(0)] int Value; [IgnoreMember] int Hidden; }` therefore gets a string-keyed formatter that serializes Hidden and ignores the declared int keys. This is wire-incompatible with the dynamic resolver and with the defining assembly's own contract.
